043package dev.visdb.seesaw.models;
044
045import java.lang.System.Logger;
046import java.sql.JDBCType;
047import java.text.FieldPosition;
048import java.text.Format;
049import java.text.ParsePosition;
050import java.text.SimpleDateFormat;
051import java.util.ArrayList;
052import java.util.EnumMap;
053import java.util.List;
054import java.util.Objects;
055
056import dev.visdb.seesaw.models.AbstractComboBoxListSwingModel.ListItem0;
057import dev.visdb.seesaw.utils.JStuff;
058
059import static dev.visdb.seesaw.utils.JStuff.sf;
060import static java.lang.System.Logger.Level.*;
061
062/**
063 * Use this to produce a string representation of an ListItem.
064 * Configure the order in which the list item elements are formatted,
065 * each element type, and optionally Format,
066 * with {@link #addElemType(int, java.sql.JDBCType, java.text.Format) }.
067 * After this object is created, by default
068 * element 0 is formatted with toString(). Start with {@link #clear()}
069 * to set up a different formatting specification.
070 * <p>
071 * Each JDBCType can have a default Format specified; use
072 * {@link #setFormat(java.sql.JDBCType, java.text.Format) }
073 * to set a Format for a type.
074 * There are preset defaults for the date/time types
075 * {@snippet :
076 * // @link substring="SimpleDateFormat" target="java.text.SimpleDateFormat" type="link" :
077 * These builtin defaults use SimpleDateFormat; the initial patterns are:
078 *    JDBCType.DATE        "yyyy-MM-dd"              ISO_LOCAL_DATE
079 *    JDBCType.TIME        "HH:mm:ss"                ISO_LOCAL_TIME
080 *    JDBCType.TIMESTAMP   "yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss"   ISO_LOCAL_DATE_TIME
081 * }
082 * When an elem is formatted, first a format assigned to the elem is checked,
083 * then the default format for the elem type is checked,
084 * if neither is available, then toString() is used to format the elem.
085 * the default time formats use .
086 * <p>
087 * Use {@link #format(java.lang.Object)}, where the argument
088 * is an ListItem, to get the String representation. Note
089 * that if format's argument is not an ListItem, then an
090 * empty String is produced.
091 * <p>
092 * This is compatible with GlazedLists AutoCompleteSupport.
093 *
094 * @since 4.0.0
095 */
096// TODO: Change to use java.time formatters.
097// TODO: API for specifying system wide defaults? Lookup?
098// TODO: interoperability with SSFormat
099@SuppressWarnings("serial")
100public class ListItemFormat extends Format {
101  //TODO: Put default formats into a common location (not in ListItemFormat).
102  /** default date format */
103  public static final String DATE_DEFAULT = "yyyy-MM-dd";
104  /** default time format */
105  public static final String TIME_DEFAULT = "HH:mm:ss";
106  /** default timestamp format */
107  public static final String TIMESTAMP_DEFAULT = "yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss";
108  /** default elem separator */
109  public static final String DEFAULT_SEPARATOR = " | ";
110  private static final FieldPosition FP0 = new FieldPosition(0);
111
112  private String separator = DEFAULT_SEPARATOR;
113  /** elemInfos.get(elemIndex) == elemInfo. */
114  protected List<ElemInfo> elemInfos = new ArrayList<>(4);
115  /** format these elem in order of List. */
116  protected List<Integer> itemElemIndexes = new ArrayList<>(4);
117
118  // allow customization of date/time formats
119  private final EnumMap<JDBCType, Format> formats = new EnumMap<>(JDBCType.class);
120
121  private static final Logger logger = JStuff.getLogger();
122
123  /**
124   * Encapsulate info about element in SSListInfo.
125   */
126  protected static class ElemInfo {
127    /** type of the elem */
128    final JDBCType type;
129    /** Format to use with this elem, may be null */
130    final Format format;
131
132    /**
133     * Type and format for an ListItem.
134     * @param type type
135     * @param format format
136     */
137    protected ElemInfo(JDBCType type, Format format) {
138      this.type = type;
139      this.format = format;
140    }
141  }
142
143  /**
144   * Create a Format. Use {@code addElemType} to specify
145   * elements, in order, that are formatted.
146   * By default, element 0 is formatted with toString()
147   */
148  @SuppressWarnings("OverridableMethodCallInConstructor")
149  public ListItemFormat() {
150    // format elment 0 with toString()
151    addElemType(0, JDBCType.NULL);
152
153    // initialize default format patterns
154    formats.put(JDBCType.DATE, new SimpleDateFormat(DATE_DEFAULT));
155    formats.put(JDBCType.TIME, new SimpleDateFormat(TIME_DEFAULT));
156    formats.put(JDBCType.TIMESTAMP, new SimpleDateFormat(TIMESTAMP_DEFAULT));
157  }
158
159  /**
160   * Clear list item element information in preparation
161   * to establish elements to format.
162   * Note that default formatting patterns are not restored.
163   */
164  public void clear() {
165    elemInfos.clear();
166    itemElemIndexes.clear();
167  }
168
169  /**
170   * Add element for formatting.Elements are formatted in
171   * the same order as they are added. If the same elemIndex
172   * is added, the previous information is discarded.
173   *
174   * @param elemIndex ListItem elemIndex for formatting
175   * @param jdbcType type of element
176   * @param format format to use for the element, may be null
177   */
178  public void addElemType(int elemIndex, JDBCType jdbcType, Format format) {
179    Objects.requireNonNull(jdbcType);
180    // first make sure there's room
181    while (elemIndex >= elemInfos.size()) {
182      elemInfos.add(null);
183    }
184    elemInfos.set(elemIndex, new ElemInfo(jdbcType, format));
185
186    // ListItem is formatted in the order the items are added
187    Integer indexAsObject = elemIndex;
188    itemElemIndexes.remove(indexAsObject);
189    itemElemIndexes.add(indexAsObject);
190  }
191
192  /**
193   * Add element for formatting.Elements are formatted in
194   * the same order as they are added. If the same elemIndex
195   * is added, the previous information is discarded.
196   * The default Format for this type is used.
197   *
198   * @param elemIndex ListItem elemIndex for formatting
199   * @param jdbcType type of element
200   */
201  public void addElemType(int elemIndex, JDBCType jdbcType) {
202    addElemType(elemIndex, jdbcType, null);
203  }
204
205  /**
206   * Set the default Format for the specified jdbc type.
207   * Only the {@link Format#format(Object, StringBuffer, java.text.FieldPosition)}
208   * method is used with the argument Format.
209   * @param jdbcType all elements of this type use the specified format
210   * @param format the format
211   * @return the previous format
212   */
213  public Format setFormat(JDBCType jdbcType, Format format) {
214    return formats.put(jdbcType, format);
215  }
216
217  /**
218   * Get the default Format for the specified JDBCType.
219   * @param jdbcType format for this
220   * @return format or null if no format has been set
221   */
222  public Format getFormat(JDBCType jdbcType) {
223    return formats.get(jdbcType);
224  }
225
226  /**
227   * The separator is goes between elements in a formatted string.
228   * @param separator the separator
229   */
230  public void setSeparator(String separator) {
231    this.separator = separator;
232  }
233
234  /**
235   * @return the separator
236   */
237  public String getSeparator() {
238    return separator;
239  }
240
241  /**
242   * This implementation does not create Object from String.
243   * @param source text
244   * @param pos pos
245   * @return the original string
246   */
247  @Override
248  public Object parseObject(String source, ParsePosition pos) {
249    // Do not create objects from here
250    return source;
251  }
252
253  /**
254   * Note that pos is ignored.
255   * @param _listItem item being formatted
256   * @param toAppendTo StringBuffer being worked on
257   * @param pos pos
258   * @return StringBuffer being worked on
259   */
260  @Override
261  public StringBuffer format(Object _listItem, StringBuffer toAppendTo, FieldPosition pos) {
262    if (_listItem != null && _listItem instanceof ListItem0) {
263      // GlazedLists guarantees only format(Object), so ignore pos.
264      ListItem0 listItem = (ListItem0) _listItem;
265      for (int i = 0; i < itemElemIndexes.size(); i++) {
266        // if this isn't the first element, add the separator
267        if (i != 0) {
268          toAppendTo.append(separator);
269        }
270        int elemIndex = itemElemIndexes.get(i);
271        appendValue(toAppendTo, elemIndex, listItem);
272      }
273    }
274    return toAppendTo;
275  }
276
277  /**
278   * This method allows overriding classes to access the list item
279   * elements directly without going through remodel.
280   *
281   * @param elemIndex index of element
282   * @param listItem container holding the element
283   * @return the element
284   */
285  protected Object getElem(int elemIndex, ListItem listItem) {
286    return ((ListItem0) listItem).getElem(elemIndex);
287  }
288
289  /**
290   * Format the indicated element, by default use toString().
291   * @param sb append string value to this
292   * @param elemIndex index of element
293   * @param listItem container holding the element
294   */
295  protected void appendValue(StringBuffer sb, int elemIndex, ListItem listItem) {
296    Object elem = getElem(elemIndex, listItem);
297    if (elem == null) {
298      return;
299    }
300
301    ElemInfo elemInfo = elemInfos.get(elemIndex);
302    JDBCType jdbcType = elemInfo.type;
303    Format format = elemInfo.format;
304    if (format == null) {
305      format = formats.get(jdbcType);
306    }
307    if (format != null) {
308      try {
309        format.format(elem, sb, FP0);
310        return;
311      } catch (Exception ex) {
312        logger.log(ERROR, sf("can't format %s with %s. Exception: %s", elem.toString(),
313                             format.toString(), ex.getMessage()));
314      }
315    }
316    // No formatter, or formatter got an exception
317    sb.append(elem.toString());
318  }
319}
